recipes.name: Too Easy Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 6 fresh peaches - pitted, skinned, and sliced

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter an 8-inch square baking dish.
Cut crust from bread slices, and cut each into 4 or 5 strips. Spread fruit into prepared pan, and cover with a layer of bread strips.
Beat together butter, sugar, and flour; mix in egg. Pour mixture over the fruit and bread.
Bake in preheated oven for 35 to 45 minutes, or until golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Too Easy Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: Fresh peaches are sliced and arranged in an 8x8-inch pan and covered with strips of white bread instead of the traditional biscuit dough.

Cut crust from bread slices, and cut each into 4 or 5 strips. Spread fruit into prepared pan, and cover with a layer of bread strips.

review.reviewBody: the recipe title says it all!!! I made this because I had some peaches I HAD to use. I took it to a party and everyone wanted the recipe. I did sprinkel a little cinnamon on top for that little something extra! Great recipe!!!

I used 1 cup of SR flour,1 cup milk,1 cup sugar,1 stick butter 1 LG can sliced peaches with thick syrup;melt butter in 10×13 baking dish while mixing other ingredients...Mix flour,sugar,milk well till butter melted,pour batter over butter then scoop peaches over batter being sure not to stir the mixture,place mixture in oven on 335% for 40-45imutes until crust is golden brown & center is done...Place Vanilla Ice Cream on top of cobbler,DELICIOUS!!!AND THIS MY FRIENDS IS KNOWN AS"LAZY GAL PEACH COBBLER"?. P/S...No worrying about trying to gather up all of the ingredients that only 1 out of 1o of us have ever heard of anyway!

Loved this, made a few changes based on other peach cobbler recipes. I tossed the peaches (I actually used nectarines) with about a 1/4 cup of sugar with cinnamon and about a tablespoon of corn starch. used about 1/2 cup sugar with 1/4 cup melted butter and the egg. tossed the bread in that mixture and layered it on top of the fruit. followed the rest of the recipe and it turned out very well.
My only change was reducing sugar and adding cinnamon to peaches and a sprinkling on top before baking. This is wonderful!

I have used this recipe many times, always with excellent results. The two things I did change, however, were adding 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract to the sugar, butter and egg mixture and I sprinkled the peaches with a little ground nutmeg before adding the bread over the peaches. This cobbler is especially good when serving it warm, but it is not too bad the next day by warming it a little in the microwave. I have also used strawberries instead of peaches, leaving off the nutmeg, and it turned out really good as well.

Wanted to get in one more dish before the Georgia peaches are gone. Followed the recipe to the letter except for reducing the sugar to 1 cup and I'll most likely reduce to 3/4 cup the next time. I think the key to the cobbler topping is using a really flavorful, good quality bread. I used Publix Bakery Homestyle Bread which is buttery, and IMO the best white bread available in this area. I tried to do a little bit of a lattice weave with the bread strips on the top which helped its presentation. The only time-consuming part of this recipe is peeling the peaches. The peach filling was juicy, and the topping buttery and crisp. Thumbs up in this house, and definitely will make again. One final comment...ain't NO way this 8x8 cobbler will feed 12. In this house, it's more like 6 (or maybe even 4, YUM).

Taking others advice, I doubled the recipe to fit a 9x13 pan, cut the sugar to 1 cup white, added 1/4 cup dark brown, 1 cup butter, 1 tbs cinnamon, used 1 loaf of bread with the crust, about 5 slices diced on the bottom, and the rest diced into small (1/2 inch) pieces for the top and poured the liquid part over the the bread. I've had to cook it for up to 90 minutes to get the nice brown look. Everyone that's had it LOVES it.

I made a few changes that previous reviewers suggested. My changes:
 whole grain bread - I like the hearty taste of wholegrain
I used a combination of nectarines and peaches, teaspoon of lemon juice to fruit to prevent browning, for texture pecans, added sprinkling of cinnamon to the fruit and also a little on top along with a sprinkling of sugar. Sugar gave a nice crunch when eating. Used 3/4 c sugar on the fruit. 
 It was amazing. Thank you to Joan.

This recipe was great! I doubled the recipe and followed some of the recommendations to cut back on the sugar, butter and flour. I used 2/3 cup of sugar, 1/2 cup butter and 4 Tbsp of whole wheat flour instead of white. I sprinkled the top with cinnamon. The result was delicious! This will be a repeat recipe for sure! I was skeptical with the white bread, but it was great for not having the time to make old fashioned crust!

REALLY GOOD - but can't give it 5 stars because with the amount of sugar in recipe, it would be WAY too sweet. I used only 1/2 cup of sugar and FRESH peaches, perfectly ripe (didn't peel them). It was sublime. Do NOT use canned peaches, but if that's all you have, then perhaps no sugar is the best solution. The bread soaked up the egg mixture and got nice and custardy and crispy. Sooooo delicious.

I will make this again, and again. Delicious and super easy to prepare. My changes were to add one teaspoon of pure vanilla extract to the batter and I only used 3/4 cup of sugar as the peaches that I used were sweet already. The bread that I used was a farmhouse style bread. As suggested, I will double the recipe the next time. Serve it with a nice scoop of vanilla ice cream!

Too sweet. Couldn’t taste the fresh peaches. If I ever made this again I’d use maybe a half cup of sugar. I had to scoop out probably 3/4 - 1 cup of the sauce after baking for 55 mins. Peaches just floating in it. Not good. Too many better recipes out there to make this again.
yes didn't have egg, so just melted butter and mixed with sugar.

This recipe is WAY too sweet for my taste. Even after cutting back on what was called for I couldn't eat it. I threw out everything but the peaches. What a way to waste some luscious fruit - and vanilla ice cream!
Terrific!! It was SO easy, and tastes great!!! I made a double batch and froze 1 but haven't eaten the frozen one yet. Hope it thaws and reheats well.
Excellent! My husband really enjoyed this. I made it with fresh peaches and didn’t change a thing.
I never saw a dessert disappear so fast. I did what others said and cut the sugar way back. The cinnamon really made it sweet all on its own.
love this recipe I used canned apricots and it worked out so good!
Made this, added a little cinnamon and nutmeg, but came out watery. Maybe add baking powder? The taste, though, was superb.

It was simple to make but didn't taste very good to me. It was weird to cook and didn't hold together in any sense of the word. It felt like I was just eating chunks of peaches and chunks of sugary dough. I won't make this again.
